correctness.rationale: The representation T_a=Σ_{k≥0}a_kR^k converges in operator norm since a∈ℓ₁ and ||R||=1. Phase-align finitely many x_{N−k} to show ||T_a||≥Σ_{k≤N}|a_k| for every N, yielding exact norm ||a||₁. For non-scalar a, first nonzero offdiagonal a_m and first nonzero coordinate x_j of an eigenvector force eigenvalue a_0 and then contradiction a_m x_j=0 in coordinate j+m, so point spectrum empty. For |z|<1, summation F_z(x)=Σz^n x_n is a nonzero adjoint eigenfunctional for R; for |z|=1, twist a shift-invariant Banach limit L((z^n x_n)) to obtain a nonzero eigenfunctional. Therefore T_a−Φ_a(z) has range inside a proper closed hyperplane and is injective, hence Φ_a(closed disk) is residual. Conversely characters on convolution algebra ℓ₁(N₀) are evaluations at |z|≤1, so outside Φ_a(closed disk) the algebraic convolution inverse gives an actual bounded inverse on ℓ∞. No tail truncation or approximate eigenvectors are mistaken for the infinite theorem. The scalar kernel exception is separately correct.
